# Additive tuning of 2026-10-31, engine round 1 best so far, scenario 2

## Run identity

```yaml
model: claude-sonnet-5
served_version: claude-sonnet-5
```

**This line is the `best` stage of round 1 of the engine layer, in the tuning round of the additive campaign that [#1877](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1877) asked for.** The plan on [#1877](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1877#issuecomment-6526205178) puts this stage second: it measures scenario 2, the documents and the engine as they stand, so that each rewording of what the engine prints has a best so far to beat. The owner accepted that plan [on the issue](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1877#issuecomment-6526210603), and [#1910](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/pull/1910) opened the layer. `tools/probe/try.sh launch` ran it from the one-line spec `additive scenario-2 tuning`. It is the `scenario-2` arm of the additive tier over the 22 probes of the tuning set, at 7 repetitions per probe, on `claude-sonnet-5` under Claude Code 2.1.288.

**One tree, one pin, one launch.** Every session ran in a fresh copy of a `git archive` of the pinned tree, and the engine of that tree. The pin was `5763a97e` for the whole batch. That commit differs from the base pin `d20eb3fd` only by [#1917](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/pull/1917), which raised the cap of this launch and changed no source of the engine. The canary of 8 sessions held 4 records that named paths outside the workspace: each ran a `find /`-style search, on the same probes and in the same pattern as the canary of the base, and the sandbox binds none of those paths. The owner read them and [passed the canary](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1877#issuecomment-6537999534) before `canary-passed` was written. The driver then halted five times on a harness failure of the kind that a usage limit causes, and it continued in the same try root at the same pin. It did not launch the batch again. The `tree` digest in the identity above is the digest the assembly recorded.

**What the recorder counted.** The line holds 144 sessions and cost 13623 cents: the intent hook live in 0, 3 stopped at the turn cap, 1 stopped at the session budget, 126 paths outside the workspace named, 0 sessions uncounted, 0 web-tool calls. 56 of the 144 sessions called the engine. A session the recorder could not count adds nothing to either count, so each count is a floor.

**Why 144 sessions and not 154.** The driver ran this try with a cap of 15000 cents and a session budget of 300 cents. At 144 of 154 sessions it had charged 14312 cents, and each of the 10 sessions left would have crossed the cap after its reservation of 300 cents, so the driver stopped as capped. The owner ruled [on the issue](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1877#issuecomment-6540711867) that the try is graded as it stands, with no raise of the cap. On that ruling the marker `capped` was renamed `capped.ruled-grade-144` and `done` was written. The 10 sessions that did not run are repetitions of probes that have other repetitions in this line, so no probe is absent from it.

**The result.** Scenario 2 passed 67 of the 144 sessions it graded. The base row compares this measurement with the base of scenario 1 at `d20eb3fd`, which passed 58 of 153 in [the base transcript](additive-tuning-of-2026-10-31-base-re-measure-of-scenario-1.md). The difference is +8.6 points, with the interval [-2.6, +19.5]. The interval includes zero, so this line does not show that the engine helps, and it does not show that the engine does not help. The keep rule reads only a confirmation, and a best so far is never kept. This line is the number that each screened rewording of the engine layer is compared with.

**The contract of this batch.** The sessions ran under the recorder contract of spec 15: a `bwrap` sandbox with no network of its own, a configuration directory that holds a copy of the credentials and nothing else, the permission mode `dontAsk`, and `WebSearch` and `WebFetch` denied. The owner approved $1,300.00 for this layer, and `.headwater/probe.yml` holds $1,300.00 for the tuning round.

**What the batch cost.** The driver charged 14312 cents against its cap, and the 144 recorded sessions account for 13623 cents of that sum. The difference is sessions that recorded nothing: sessions that the harness halted, and re-tries after a refusal. `try.sh spent` counts the 14312 cents against the base ceiling of 25000 cents, and not against the ceiling of 105000 cents for the tries. With the 12373 cents of the base, the base ceiling now stands at 26685 cents, 1685 cents over it. The owner named that sum in the ruling to grade this try.

**Where the raw recordings are.** The raw session logs are outside git, under `/mnt/build/hw-1877/engine-r1-best/a/sessions/L1-*/raw.jsonl` on the host that ran the batch. Nobody deletes them until the report of [#1779](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1779) is published.

**Where the other figures are.** The rate and the interval of each probe are in the generated result that reads this transcript.

    - tool: "SendMessage"
      argument: "{\"to\":\"main\",\"summary\":\"Research on cites_evidence vs body-link rule and obligations\",\"message\":\"**(1) No exact rule exists.** No implemented check matches \\\"body links to evaluation X, X absent from `cites_evidence`.\\\" The 50 rules in `engine/crates/check/src/lib.rs` (RULES array) contain nothing of this shape. Closest-named candidates and why they don't match:\\n- `relation.reciprocity.missing` (`engine/crates/check/src/reciprocity.rs:77`) — checks that an *already-declared* `cites_evidence`/`cited_by` pair has both ends written; doesn't look at body prose at all.\\n- `warrant.evidence.unsupported` (`engine/crates/check/src/basis.rs:154`) — checks that a doc claiming `evidence_basis: evidenced` doesn't point (via the `evidence` relation family, which includes `cites_evidence`) at a target whose `warrant` is `asserted`. Different question entirely.\\n- `link.path.unresolved`, `link.fragment.unresolved`, `link.identifier.mismatch` — about dead/mismatched links, not missing declarations.\\n\\nSpec 4 (`docs/spec/04-assurance-model.md:85`) *describes* a rule for exactly this shape, calling it the **\\\"undeclared reference\\\" check**, but it is not among the 50 implemented RULES — it's aspirational prose, not shipped code.\\n\\n**(2) Spec language.** `docs/spec/04-assurance-model.md:85` (the key quote): \\\"Q4 keeps relation semantics out of prose, so a link in the body asserts nothing that the engine can check. The **undeclared reference** check narrows the gap that this leaves. A prose link that resolves to a corpus document with which the source declares no relation raises an advisory finding. The author wrote the reference once, and the fix writes the declaration.\\\" Line 87: the fix is mechanical \\\"only when exactly one enabled relation type permits the pair of kinds at the two ends\\\"; otherwise it's judgment, no patch. Line 87 also notes there's **no converse check**: \\\"A declared relation whose target the prose never names is not a finding.\\\" So the spec never claims `cites_evidence` must be *exhaustive* over body links in the strict sense of a blocking/error rule — it frames the gap as advisory-only and not-yet-built. Spec 3 (`docs/spec/03-authoring-and-lifecycle.md:168-184`) defines `evidence_basis`/warrant semantics but says nothing about body-link-vs-`cites_evidence` consistency. Spec 12 doesn't address this at all.\\n\\n**(3) Nearest obligation.** `docs/obligations/0055-the-tradition-has-no-relation-for-the-link-that-this-corpus.md` (HW-OBL-0055, status: current, waiting_on: ruling) — \\\"No relation admits a specification-to-specification or an evaluation-to-specification pair... Under Q4 every one of those prose links is an advisory finding with no fix, because the author has nothing to declare.\\\" This is the general ancestor of your gap but is about relation *vocabulary* gaps, not a specific doc's `cites_evidence` omission. `docs/obligations/0181-...md` (HW-OBL-0181, discharged) is a different defect class (dead path links never becoming findings) — close in shape, not in substance. No obligation names the specific spec-12/owl-skos-worked-example gap.\\n\\n**(4) Filing pattern.** This kind of low-stakes drift (stale cross-reference, missing cites_evidence edge) is typically folded into a **batch obligation**, not filed standalone. `docs/obligations/0235-eleven-documents-and-edges-that-trail-a-change-of-run-20261002-1233.md` is the template: it bundles ~13 unrelated stale-sentence/missing-edge findings from one maintenance run under one record, explicitly ruled \\\"RECORD and not an issue\\\" because \\\"None stops an adopter.\\\" One of its bullets is structurally identical to your case: \\\"`docs/spec/05-ai-integration.md` ... declares no `traces_to` or `cites_evidence` edge onto `docs/spec/15-the-recorder-contract.md`.\\\" So precedent favors adding your spec-12/owl-skos item to a similar batch record (or the next one in that series) rather than minting a new standalone HW-OBL-XXXX.\\n\\nNote for context: `docs/spec/13-open-obligations.md:21-23` correctly lists `HW-EVAL-owl-skos-worked-example` under its own `cites_evidence` — confirming other docs that link to that evaluation in body do declare it, which underlines that spec 12's omission is a genuine, if minor, instance of the drift class HW-OBL-0055/0235 already track.\",\"type\":\"message\",\"recipient\":\"main\",\"content\":\"**(1) No exact rule exists.** No implemented chec…\"}"
      result: ""

Report back in detail (can be long, this is for planning).\\n\\nCONTEXT: There's a decision record docs/decisions/0045-coloring-the-cli-and-where-the-banner-goes.md (id HW-DR-0045, status: current) that rules on two things: (1) terminal color rules (ANSI palette, per-stream sensing, --no-color/NO_COLOR), and (2) a masthead \\\"banner\\\" that prints on the root help screen only, with --no-banner/HEADWATER_NO_BANNER flags to suppress it. I need to produce a NEW decision that keeps the color rules but removes the banner entirely (no banner on ANY screen, not even root help) — effectively reverting/undoing the banner part while keeping the color part intact.\\n\\nQuestions:\\n1. Read docs/decisions/README.md header/footer and a couple of representative files to find the conventions for \\\"superseding\\\" a decision: does this corpus ever edit a `status: current` decision file in place and change its content, or does it always add a NEW decision record file that states `status: current`, with `relations: supersedes: [HW-DR-00NN]`, while the OLD file's status is updated to `superseded`? Look at concrete examples where one decision supersedes another (e.g. grep front matter for \\\"supersedes\\\" across docs/decisions/*.md) and show me 2 full front-matter examples of supersession, including what happens to the OLD file's own status/body (is the old file's body left untouched, or does it get a note added?).\\n2. What is the next available decision number after 0113 (list the actual filenames sorted numerically to confirm the true max, since the shelf README.md is \\\"headwater:generated\\\" and may list them out of numeric order)?\\n3. Find every file in the repo (docs/**, engine/**, site/**, any shelf) that mentions \\\"banner\\\", \\\"NO_BANNER\\\", \\\"no_banner\\\", \\\"no-banner\\\", \\\"masthead\\\" — give me full file paths grouped by directory, with 1-line description of what each reference says (e.g. \\\"interface contract Options table row for --no-banner\\\", \\\"Rust code implementing banner()\\\", \\\"test asserting banner text\\\"). I need a complete inventory since all of it may need to change together.\\n4. Read engine/crates/cli/src/paint.rs and engine/crates/cli/src/lib.rs and engine/crates/cli/src/main.rs — specifically every function/field/constant related to banner (banner(), banner_of, NO_BANNER global, no_banner field, first_screen banner insertion). Give me exact line numbers and short code excerpts so I know what to delete/modify.\\n5. Find engine/crates/cli/tests/help.rs and tests/width.rs (or wherever banner behavior is tested) — what test cases exist for the banner, with line numbers.\\n6. Is there a \\\"decision register\\\" (HW-LIB-decision-record doctrine, or docs/process/decisions vs docs/decisions distinction) that states rules about HOW a decision must be retired/superseded — e.g. must the superseding decision literally use the word \\\"supersedes\\\" in relations, must it keep governs edges, etc? Check docs/spec/ for anything about decision-record kind requirements (required facets, supersedes relation symmetry, \\\"new writes no far half\\\" decision 0101 — does creating decision N that supersedes M require ALSO writing something on M, or does `headwater check --fix` do that automatically?).\\n7. Are there any OBLIGATIONS (docs/obligations/*.md) or OPEN QUESTIONS (docs/spec/09-open-questions.md) that reference HW-DR-0045 or the banner, which might need updating too?\\n8. Check docs/interfaces/headwater-help.md specifically — what does it currently say about the banner (full relevant section)?\\n\\nReport concisely but completely — I need exact file paths, line numbers, and short quotes, organized by question number.\"}"
